messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: elevated client error rate detected in us-central-1 starting at 2613456720. Smart routing (policy: smart-route-v2) began cross-region fallback to eu-central and swapped to variant-legacy. Paging oncall.

leah: multiple tenants reporting 504/timeouts. I'm seeing repeated retry waves in the traces: client retries (n=3, fixed 500ms) cause each failed request to re-enter routing and trigger fallback again -> traffic doubles each retry wave.

matt: confirmed. routing metrics show primary variant (variant-fast) in us-central intermittently overflowing; fallback chooses variant-legacy in eu-central which has much slower p95. Clients don't backoff so failover load amplifies.

devin: paging @oncall-olivia. this is user-facing. please pick up.

oncall-olivia: oncall here. quick triage: router queue in us-central spiked from 50->900 in 90s. failover threshold 150, so cascade happened. in-flight retries visible for ~3 minutes causing repeated spikes to eu-central.

leah: root cause hypothesis: a recent autoscaler change allowed starting up new variant instances slower than before, leading to temporary capacity holes. smart-route-v2's probe window is short (5s) so fallback is aggressive.

matt: added context: variant-legacy was recently reintroduced as fallback because it has better cold-start behavior for some customers. but its execution time is 2-3x under load.

devin: mitigation idea list:
1) set smart-route-v2 to local-only for 15m
2) change fallback probe window to 30s and add a rate limit for fallback QPS
3) soft-fail at router with 429 when queue>120
4) advertise `x-retry-suggest: backoff` header to SDKs
5) temporarily blacklist variant-legacy for fallback
6) hot scale variant-fast in us-central +4

oncall-olivia: applying 1 and 5 now.

```
redwoodctl routing update --policy smart-route-v2 \ 
  --set allow_cross_region_fallback=false,blocked_variants=variant-legacy
```

ops-bot: routing policy updated (op: op-cc342). propagation ~10s.

leah: after flip, failovers to eu-central dropped ~92%. inbound errors decreasing but still seeing retry tail.

matt: applying a router soft-fail rule and inject header for SDKs that honor it:
```
redwoodctl router configure --region us-central-1 \ 
  --max-queue 120 --overload-behavior soft-fail --overload-code 429
redwoodctl router set-header --region us-central-1 --name x-retry-suggest --value backoff
```

ops-bot: router config update queued (deploy shards: 2/3 applied). header injection ok.

devin: recommend we also extend routing decision TTL to 20s so new requests don't keep bouncing between variants.

leah: applying TTL change:
```
redwoodctl routing set-ttl --policy smart-route-v2 --ttl-seconds 20
```

ops-bot: TTL update complete.

oncall-olivia: scaling variant-fast in us-central now:
```
redwoodctl scale cluster variant-fast --region us-central-1 --add 4
```

ops-bot: scale job started (sj-7741). provisioning nodes.

matt: note: some clients ignore headers and still retry aggressively. we should publish a deprecation on fixed-interval retry configs in SDKs.

leah: temporary customer banner posted: "We're investigating timeouts in us-central. Mitigations in progress to stabilize requests. We'll update within 15 minutes." keeping it short.

customer-success: received initial reports from two large accounts; offering post-incident call. they asked whether SDKs will get a backoff signal.

devin: status update: 5xx peaked at ~15% for some tenants, now down to ~2.8% after policy changes and router limits. scale nodes reporting healthy and serving traffic.

matt: recommendation for re-enable fallback later: use a throttled-fallback with max-fallback-qps and a probe of 60s, plus prefer warm variants.

leah: agree. follow-ups: 
- implement rate-limited fallback in smart-route-v2
- add circuit-breaker that returns 429 early instead of cascading failover
- update SDKs to respect `x-retry-suggest` and default to jittered exponential backoff
- increase probe windows before variant swap
- run a chaos test for variant swap under load

oncall-olivia: creating postmortem ticket and assigning owners: routing (leah), sdk-retries (matt), autoscaler (devin), customer-comm (customer-success). capturing logs and traces.

customer-success: customers updated; one asked for timeline and root cause details. we've scheduled a follow-up.

leah: closing incident as mitigated. will reopen if errors climb back. nice quick coordination everyone. :white_check_mark:
